rule.description: A field interface that bundles buffer-shape capabilities with value-mutation (set) and value-reading (get) capabilities, forcing implementors that are read-only or non-scalar to supply throwing stub implementations of members they do not use.

checks.description: Implementors of the fat IField interface forced to declare throw-stub value-access members they cannot support.
checks.detected_relation: implementor -> unsupported required field-interface capability (set / no-arg get) provided as a throw stub
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The IField interface exceeds these consumers' dependency boundaries by coupling buffer shape with value mutation and value reading; read-only computed fields and the struct container must depend on members they will never exercise.

matches.evidence: StructType (a field container, not a scalar value) implements fat IField, whose get():unknown/no-arg read capability forces StructType.get to throw when read with no field name.
StructType implements fat IField, whose set():unknown mutator capability forces StructType to declare a set(value) that unconditionally throws, although a struct cannot hold a scalar value.
BaseSizeOf (size-of computed field base for SizeOf8/16/32) implements fat IField, whose set() mutator forces a throw-stub set even though size-of fields are read-only offsets of another field's size.
SizeOf64Type (64-bit size-of computed field) implements fat IField, whose set() mutator forces a throw-stub set on a field that only reports another target's size.
BasePointer (pointer computed field base for Pointer8/16/32) implements fat IField, whose set() mutator forces a throw-stub set even though pointers are read-only offsets into a target struct.
Pointer64Type (64-bit pointer computed field) implements fat IField, whose set() mutator forces a throw-stub set on a field that only reports a target struct's deep offset.
